headlines.title: Valkyries beat the Dream 67-62 to even the WNBA Finals at 2-2
headlines.description: Gabby Williams scored 17 points and Golden State played stellar defense to beat the Atlanta Dream 67-62 on Saturday and even the WNBA Finals at 2-2. The best-of-seven series moves back to California on Monday for Game 5. The Valkyries stymied Atlanta star Angel Reese, holding her to just eight points. She had dominated the previous two games, averaging 25.5 points and 14 rebounds in the Dream victories. Reese struggled in Game 4, missing 10 of her 12 shots, including a few layups in the fourth quarter, after having double-doubles in each of the first three games. Atlanta trimmed a 16-point halftime deficit to 61-55 midway through the fourth quarter, bringing fans in the sellout crowd of over 17,000 to their feet. Golden State answered with a 3-pointer by Veronica Burton to briefly silence them. The Dream then scored seven of the next nine points, including a three-point play by Rhyne Howard with 28 seconds left to get within 66-62. Burton then made the first of two free throws a second later and Atlanta couldn’t convert on the other end. Howard finished with 19 points to lead Atlanta. THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. Check back for updates. AP’s earlier story follows below. The Golden State Valkyries are still confident. Trailing 2-1 in the best-of-seven WNBA Finals against Atlanta, they know a win on Saturday will give them back home-court advantage with a trip to “Ballhalla” awaiting. “It would be silly to overreact right now,” Valkyries guard Veronica Burton said. “We continue to point out the things where we lack discipline and where we lack maybe paying attention to their personnel. We address that and not overreact but also understand that there is a major sense of urgency, and we can’t necessarily wait for anything to change.” Still, the Valkyries can ill afford to lose Game 4 after getting routed in Game 3. While it’s only the second year that the WNBA has played a best-of-seven championship series, history in the NBA isn’t on the side of teams trailing 3-1. Only the 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers were able to come back from a 3-1 deficit in the Finals. For the Valkyries to have any chance, they’ll need to find a way to contain Angel Reese. Reese, who was traded to Atlanta from Chicago in the offseason, has made the most of her first postseason appearance since coming into the league three years ago. She became only the second player in finals history with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in consecutive games, joining A’ja Wilson. At 24 years old, she also became the youngest with three straight double-doubles in the finals. Reese has a really talented group around her in Jordin Canada, Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray, who has been dealing with a hand injury suffered in the semifinals.

headlines.title: Bay Area referee and umpire shortage impacting youth sports
headlines.description: A shortage of referees and umpires is impacting youth sports in the Bay Area. But a South Bay man who will be in the national spotlight and locals hope he will inspire more people to sign up to become officials for amateur sports and address the shortage. Gabe Morales, who graduated from Santa Teresa High School and Santa Clara University before heading off to umpire school, will be the home plate umpire for Friday’s Game 1 of the MLB World Series. For those involved in Bay Area amateur sports, the hope is young people see Morales on one of the biggest stages and be inspired. NBC Bay Area’s Damian Trujillo has more in the video above.

headlines.title: 911 emergency dispatch systems restored in Oakland
headlines.description: Oakland’s 911 system is back up and running as intended following the restoration of the city’s phone service Friday morning. The entire emergency dispatch system for police and fire services went down at about 8:30 p.m. Wednesday after somebody damaged AT&T fiber optic cables in an apparent copper wire theft. The city’s IT teams worked with AT&T to get the computer-aided system and internet back online Thursday evening, but repairs to the phone lines took until Friday morning to complete. During the outage, 911 calls were routed through the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office while OPD dispatchers were relocated to the Oakland Fire Department Dispatch Center and the sheriff’s dispatch center. The Fire Department’s dispatchers were able to handle all fire and medical calls for service and the county was answering 911 calls and relaying information to OPD dispatchers stationed at the Fire Department. The city has contingency plans for just such a situation but “unfortunately both of the initial fallback plans were compromised last night,” Oakland police Chief James Beere said Thursday. Oakland Oct 22 Sheng Thao Oct 23 Oakland Oct 22 Oakland tenants allege harassment by property manager, say complaints went unaddressed

headlines.title: Cut cables disrupted Oakland 911 for more than 24 hours. How could this happen?
headlines.description: After damage to AT&T fiber and copper lines disrupted several critical Oakland communications systems from Wednesday night into Friday morning, questions remain about how the city’s 911 system failed — and whether it could happen again. “Why is this so easy [to] access to [the] public,” asked @aludeurquiza on Instagram. “Isn’t something this sensitive supposed to be protected in some way,” asked @streldunn. “How will this be prevented in the future? It is absolutely unacceptable how long this took to be resolved,” said @garrettnoodle. AT&T told NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit that damage to fiber and copper lines Wednesday evening interrupting multiple critical Oakland systems for over 24 hours. The outage affected Oakland’s 911 and non-emergency phone lines, the Fire Department’s 911 system and internet and computer-aided dispatch software at OPD’s dispatch center. All services were back to normal Friday morning around 8:30 a.m., according to police. One of the first questions asked during a police press conference on Thursday: What happened to the systems’ backup plans? “Regards to the 911 line, we do have some fallback plans,” Oakland Police Chief James Beere said during a press conference on Thursday. “Unfortunately, both the initial fallback plans were compromised…so we had to fall back on our outside partner, which is the Alameda County Sheriff’s Department.” Beere offered this insight on Thursday, but the police department declined the Investigative Unit’s request for an interview on Friday to ask additional questions. The department cited the active investigation. Questions remain about why both fallback systems failed and whether the affected AT&T lines should have been better protected. The chief suggested that the damage may have involved more than an attempt to steal copper wiring. “I would say this is more of a bad actor than vandalism, particularly just because there’s more than one line and the amount of damage that was done,” he said on Thursday. During the outage, 911 calls in Oakland were routed to the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office and OPD said officers would only respond to Priority 1 calls, including incidents involving violence or immediate threat to life or serious injury. NBC Bay Area asked disaster experts what might have happened if a major earthquake had struck while Oakland’s communications systems were down. They said it could look a lot like Thursday, only worse. “We tell people not to expect to be even able to make a phone call,” said Mark Benthien with the Statewide California Earthquake Center. Benthien and Angie Lux with the Berkeley Seismology Laboratory said if a major earthquake triggered severe damage, communications systems could be down for days even weeks – similar to what happened in Oakland but on a larger scale. “To be honest, [this was] terrible, but it’s a good preparation for what could be a reality following a major earthquake,” Lux said. “This is also emphasizing the importance of community preparedness,” Benthien said. “So, knowing your neighbors, knowing the resources in your community, like on your block.” For information on how to be prepared before, during and after a major earthquake: www.EarthquakeCountry.org. Candice Nguyen is the Senior Investigative Reporter on this story. If you have a comment or a question, email her at candice.nguyen@nbcuni.com.

headlines.title: New wine country sculpture pays tribute to Robert Louis Stevenson
headlines.description: The author and poet Robert Louis Stevenson spent only a couple months in the Bay Area’s wine country back in 1880 — but that visit resulted in schools, a park, museums named for him. And now, a bronze sculpture will also bear witness to the writer’s visit. Saint Helena resident Eric Hanson and sculptor Garr Ugalde plan to unveil a new bench and sculpture of the writer, his wife and dog on November 7 in front of its new home outside the Calistoga Depot, the same train station Stevenson traveled through on his honeymoon. “We found that Robert Louis Stevenson, his wife Fanny, and his dog Chuchu came into this exact spot where I’m standing here, May of 1880,” said Hanson, standing in front of a historic train car in front of the depot. The Scottish author spent a couple years in California between 1879 and 1880, vying for the affections of his future wife. A rendering of the bench and sculptures of Robert Louis Stevenson, his wife Fanny and their dog Chuchu. During the couple’s trip to the wine country they stayed in an abandoned bunkhouse at the Silverado Mine on Mount St. Helena. It inspired his travel memoir, the Silverado Squatters. Among the many sites named for Stevenson in wine country was Robert Louis Stevenson Middle School in St. Helena, directly across the street from Hanson’s home. “Kids would be out there sitting on my split rail fence which really wasn’t that strong,” Hanson said. Hanson got the idea to save his fence by putting a bench in front of it where school kids could sit. But then the idea began to percolate — he got the idea to add a sculpture of Robert Louis Stevenson as an educational nod to the school. A rendering of the bench and sculptures of Robert Louis Stevenson, his wife Fanny and their dog Chuchu. The idea ruminated in his head for seven years until during a New Years Eve party, he struck up a conversation with Ugalde who happened to be a sculptor. “I asked him about how long have you been thinking about this project? And he said seven years,” Ugalde remembered. “I said ‘well then what are you waiting for?’” The pair came up with renderings of the bench and sculpture and tried to find a place in St. Helena to place it. But after meetings with the parks department and other groups went nowhere, they decided to see if nearby Calistoga might be interested. A planning commissioner suggested they seek a private site to avoid a lot of red tape. They pitched the idea to Michael Madden, owner of the Calistoga Depot which he transformed into a restaurant and bar. He immediately gave the project a green light. “This idea of having a monument of he and his wife and dog with luggage getting on the train,” Madden said. “The exact train that they themselves had gotten on to get up here back in those days — it seems like a perfect tie-in.” Eric Hanson shows the spot where the new Robert Louis Stevenson bench and sculpture will sit in front of the Calistoga Depot. Hanson and Ugalde raised money for the project through private donations and grants. The sculpture, which Ugalde designed, is currently getting fabricated by a team of artists at American Fine Art Foundry in Burbank. It envisions Stevenson sitting on a bench with a notebook in hand, while his new bride Fanny Vendergrift Osbourne stands over him, as the couple’s dog Chuchu looks up. Hanson hopes the sculpture will become a portal of curiosity for visitors who encounter it. “It’s a spot on the bench where people can sit and have an Instagram moment,” Hanson said. “And become part of history instead of just observe it from afar.” Marin County Sep 15 9/11 Sep 11 While the initial sculpture was to only feature Stevenson, Hanson and Uglade said their research about Fanny and her impact on the writer’s life suggested her omission would’ve cut out a key chapter of the story. “His wife was a really a driving force in his life,” Ugalde said. “She would get the first reads of everything he wrote, she was his first editor and she was actually the one that convinced him to start writing fiction.” The sculpture will sit in front of an original set of railcars — the actual ones the writer rode when he made the trek to Calistoga. While the town’s original population of 500 has since grown to 5000, Hanson said it still retains the same character as it did when Stevenson visited. “It just enhances the story of Calistoga and the reason Robert Louis Stevenson came here back in the 1880s is still here today,” Hanson said. “We still have the hot springs here, the mineral baths and we still have the wine and we still have the same landscape.”

headlines.title: A new $1.5M fund will pay you back if a thief drained your gift card
headlines.description: Consumers whose gift cards suddenly lost value might be able to recover some of their money thanks to a new, seven-figure restitution fund. The San Francisco City Attorney says his office has reached a deal with InComm, the company that sells Vanilla gift cards. Many NBC and Telemundo viewers told us back in 2022 and 2023 that their Vanilla gift card balances vanished. “I have no idea what happened to it,” said Walnut Creek resident Sydney Polich when she spoke with NBC Bay Area. “I knew there was money left on it. But it was declined.” Thieves were tampering with the barcodes on all kinds of gift cards, then easily taking people’s money. Some viewers didn’t get their money back from Vanilla until they contacted NBC Responds or Telemundo Responde. San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu’s office then sued Vanilla’s parent, InComm Payments, claiming “insufficient security for Vanilla cards.” The complaint even mentions NBC coverage a few times. “We heard about this over and over, which is why we filed the lawsuit,” said San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu. “I’m really glad that we [now] have a resolution that will hopefully get consumers some, if not all, of the money they lost.” Chiu says InComm and the City or San Francisco have agreed to settle the suit. The deal includes a new $1.525 million fund for consumers. If you bought or got a Vanilla gift card in California between November 1, 2019 and September 30, 2024 and were unable to spend some or all of the money loaded on it, you might be eligible for restitution. “Folks have to do this by February 19th of next year,” Chiu said. “Our hope is that we can get a substantial number of Californians who were victims of this consumer scam some or all of their money back.” In a statement, InComm said, “Although the San Francisco City Attorney’s lawsuit against InComm Payments was misguided, we are pleased to have worked with his office to resolve the matter and put the litigation behind us.” To apply for a slice of the $1.525 million settlement, go to cagiftcardsettlement.com. Before applying, consider searching your records. The settlement website says providing proof of your loss can help. Look for info like your card number or card serial number. Also, if you complained to InComm, see if they gave you a claim you can now share.

headlines.title: Sea lion safely removed from road in Hayward
headlines.description: A sea lion was safely removed from a roadway in Hayward on Thursday afternoon. Police said they responded to a report of a seal in the middle of a roadway near Breakwater Avenue at 12:42 p.m. There, officers and Animal Control ensured the sea lion was safe until the Marine Mammal Center could assist further, authorities said. Hayward police stated the officers shared playful moments with the sea lion while waiting for assistance.

headlines.title: Defense cross-examines FBI agent in Sheng Thao corruption trial
headlines.description: An FBI agent returned to the stand Friday in the corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao. The defense got its first chance to challenge FBI Special Agent Kathrine Barclay’s testimony in federal court in Oakland. For the past two days, Barclay has laid out what prosecutors say is evidence connecting Thao to a bribery and wire fraud scheme with her co-defendants: Thao’s longtime partner Andre Jones and businessmen David and Andy Duong, who own California Waste Solutions, Oakland’s recycling contractor. Sheng Thao Oct 22 Sheng Thao Oct 19 Sheng Thao Oct 14 Barclay testified that texts between businessman Mario Juarez and Andy Duong included drafts of negative mailers targeting Loren Taylor, who ran against Thao in the race for mayor. Juarez allegedly confirmed he bought the website TaylorFraud.com. Barclay also pointed to a financial trail showing the Duongs’ California Waste Solutions paid Juarez $75,000, the amount linked to the mailer campaign. Text messages also appear to outline what prosecutors say was the broader deal: cash and help getting Thao elected in exchange for 300 modular housing units, a 10-year city contract extension for California Waste Solutions and influence over city department appointments. Barclay on Friday continued to testify about the texts investigators found between Thao and Jones. The texts included messages about trouble paying rent and a $6,000 payment to restore their power. Prosecutors also played a 2019 call in which Thao appears to share details of a closed-session meeting about alleged overcharging by California Waste Solutions, with Andy Duong, whose family owns the company. In a 2023 call, then-Mayor Thao vents to Andy Duong about Councilmembers Janani Ramachandran and Treva Reid criticizing her trade mission to Vietnam, telling him he will have to pick a side. Prosecutors also showed a video of Juarez toasting to starting Evolutionary Homes with the Duongs — one of the businesses prosecutors claim was central to the pay for play deal between the Duongs and Thao. Andy Dong’s attorney Erik Babcock argues the images are prejudicial. Babcock also challenged the link between a $75,000 CWS check and a negative campaign mailer campaign. He also raised questions about the credibility of Juarez, who pleaded guilty in the case and is testifying in hopes of getting a lighter sentence. Andy Duong’s attorney argues there is no audio proof his client bribed Thao and said there is no evidence the Duongs ever got any of the city contracts or contract extensions prosecutors claim were part of the deal. But prosecutors say simply pursing a “pay for access” deal is a crime, even if it ultimately fell apart. The defense’s cross-examination of Barclay continues Monday.

headlines.title: More than 20 vehicles damaged in San Jose carport fire
headlines.description: More than 20 vehicles were damaged after a fire ripped through a carport early Friday at a San Jose condominium complex, firefighters said. Emergency crews responded around 2:01 a.m. to the 200 block of Shadow Run Drive following reports of a vehicle fire. The blaze destroyed a detached carport and left vehicles with varying degrees of damage. The heat from the fire was so intense, it cracked windows in nearby homes. No injuries were reported, and no nearby structures were involved. No residents were displaced. The fire was under control by 3:03 a.m. Meanwhile, residents are left trying to process the aftermath of a fire that left so many cars beyond repair. An investigation is ongoing. San Jose Oct 22 San Jose Oct 22 San Jose Oct 22

headlines.title: Ceremony honors former SFPD Deputy Chief Ann Mannix and daughter
headlines.description: The San Francisco Police Department memorialized former Deputy Chief Ann Mannix and her daughter Katie with a full honor guard ceremony on Friday. Ann Mannix died at the hands of her estranged husband, Kevin Mannix, who also shot their 24-year-old daughter before turning the gun on himself in Strawberry, Marin County. Investigators say the couple had been going through a divorce. Ann Mannix spent 34 years with the San Francisco Police Department, retiring as a deputy chief. She rose through the ranks of the department, becoming the first woman to join and then lead the SWAT team. “Ann really got out there and made the most of her career,” former SFPD Interim Chief Toney Chaplin said. “She was a fierce advocate for women in law enforcement and for women getting roles they were traditionally denied.” Mannix’s 24-year-old daughter, Katie, was studying to be a nurse like her older sister, according to the San Francisco Chronicle. San Francisco Oct 15 Marin County Oct 11 Marin County Oct 12 Mayor Daniel Lurie, Police Chief Derrik Lew, District Attorney Brooke Jenkins and first responders from multiple city agencies gathered to pay tribute to the fallen. They were standing at attention for the San Francisco Police Motorcade as it approached Saint Ignatius Church at the University of San Francisco. They escorted two hearses: the first carried Mannix. The second carried Katie. During the funeral mass, family outlined the legacy the two women now leave behind. “She was a mentor to me, my sisters, my friends, and young men and women of the San Francisco Police Department,” Ann Mannix’s son Kevin Mannix said. “My baby sister was the best friend my mom blessed me with in 2001. She is spunky, beautiful, smart, kind and always keeps you on your toes,” Ann Mannix’s daughter Lauren Mannix said. During the services, Ann Mannix’s brother, retired Police Commander Rich Correia, highlighted her ascent through the department, opening doors for other women along the way. “My sister had finesse and grace. She would float into a room with a gait of confidence and a smile of approachability,” Correia said. These full ceremonial memorials from the San Francisco Police Department are rare events. And this one is even more unusual because it’s honoring a former command staff member of the department and her civilian daughter. Mother and daughter will be buried on Saturday.

headlines.title: Crash in San Jose leaves bicyclist with life-threatening injuries
headlines.description: A cyclist suffered life-threatening injuries in a crash in San Jose on Thursday night, according to the police department. Authorities said the crash was reported at 7:24 p.m. in the area of Altamara Avenue and Moncucco Way. According to police, the bicyclist was taken to a local hospital while the driver involved remained on the scene. Police said Altamara Avenue from Pinotin Court to Eldiva Court will be blocked off for a significant amount of time. Officials advised the public to drive with caution and use alternate routes.

headlines.title: 2 active tuberculosis cases linked to San Francisco strip club, officials say
headlines.description: Thursday, the San Francisco Department of Public Health confirmed it is looking into two active cases of tuberculosis “associated with The Crazy Horse establishment in San Francisco.” The Crazy Horse is a strip club on Market Street that’s been in existence for more than three decades. The department told NBC Bay Area that it was notified of the first confirmed case in early October, and then began contact tracing efforts to identify people who may have been exposed. “These efforts are ongoing and at this time, the risk to the general public is low,” the department said in a statement. “If this status changes, we will let the public know.” Tuberculosis (or TB) is an infectious disease caused by bacteria. To contract it, health experts say, you will need to have prolonged exposure to a contagious person. Dr. Abraar Karan, who is a member of the Infectious Diseases faculty at Stanford, explained that the bacteria that cause tuberculosis are airborne. “The bacteria can hang around in the air long after someone is no longer in that space,” Karan added. “Spaces that are crowded with poor ventilation or where you have very close contact with someone that is contagious are going to be higher risk for transmission,” explained Karan explained that there are two types of tuberculosis: active and latent. Most people who contract tuberculosis get latent tuberculosis and do not show symptoms, and are not immediately contagious. However, over time and without treatment, that person can develop active tuberculosis, which is contagious and a serious illness. The symptoms of active tuberculosis can include fever, coughing, weight loss, and night sweats, Karan noted. Dr. Peter Chin-Hong, a Professor of Medicine and Infectious Disease Specialist at UCSF, believes the SFDPH contact tracing teams will be tracking these cases for a while because the bacteria that causes tuberculosis grows very slowly. “They’ll do testing and probably repeat the testing in a few weeks, because again, sometimes the testing may be negative, but because [the bacteria] grows so slowly, eventually that test may turn positive if there was a true infection,” he noted. Chin-Hong also cautioned: these two cases don’t automatically mean there is an outbreak. “[Public Health officials] have to establish at least two cases that are linked, and we’re not even sure at this point whether the two cases are actually acquired at the establishment, or they got it somewhere else,” Chin-Hong said. He noted that the San Francisco Department of Health will be assessing who is most at risk and contacting them. The San Francisco Department of Public Health said it is important for people at risk of tuberculosis to get tested and treated. NBC Bay Area reached out to Crazy Horse for comment, but has not received a response.
